metadata.defaultTitle: ATS readability — see your CV the way the parser does
metadata.description: Read a CV the way an applicant tracking system reads it: what parses, what is missing, and which terms from the job ad never appear. Runs entirely in the browser.
metadata.openGraphDescription: See your CV the way the parser does. Nothing is uploaded.

common.disclaimer: The checks are heuristics built from how mainstream parsers behave, not a reproduction of any named vendor. A good score means nothing is standing between your CV and a human reader; it is not a prediction that you will be invited.

home.headline: Your CV is read as text, not as a design.
home.lede: An applicant tracking system throws away your layout and keeps whatever text it can pull out. This shows you that text, scores what survived out of 100, and lists what to change — ordered by how many points each fix is worth.
home.privacyNote: The file is read in your browser and scored there. It is never uploaded.
home.methodIntro: Each dimension starts at its full weight and loses points only to a named finding, so the report can always tell you where a missing point went.
home.methodNoBlackBox: Nothing here is a black box: every deduction names the line it came from and what to write instead.

parseability.name: Parseability
parseability.what: Whether the text layer survives extraction at all: columns, tables, icon fonts, broken encodings.

keywords.name: Keyword match
keywords.what: Coverage of the terms mined from the job ad, weighted by how central each one is to the posting.

impact.name: Impact
impact.what: Quantified results and ownership verbs, measured against responsibility filler.

structure.name: Structure
structure.what: Headings a parser can map to fields, dated entries in reverse order, bullets instead of paragraphs.

contact.name: Contact
contact.what: The identity fields every system stores: name, email, phone, location, profile link.

analyze.heading: See what the parser gets
analyze.lede: Upload the exact file you send to employers. The text below is what an applicant tracking system would extract — correct it if the extraction went wrong, then score it against the ad.

login.heading: Sign in
login.lede: Your CV is read and scored in your browser. The account only keeps your share links.

messages.invalidCredentials: That email and password do not match an account.
messages.signupFailed: The account could not be created. Check the address and try again.
messages.checkYourEmail: Account created. Confirm your email address to sign in.
messages.linkExpired: That confirmation link is no longer valid. Sign in to have a new one sent.

notFound.heading: Nothing here
notFound.body: A shared report lives for 30 days and then deletes itself. This one has either expired or never existed.

analyzer.cvLede: Upload the exact file you send to employers. Whatever comes out below is what a parser gets.
analyzer.extractedLabel: Extracted text — edit it if something is off
analyzer.extractedPlaceholder: Paste the CV text here if you would rather not upload a file.
analyzer.adLede: Optional, and the single biggest change to the result. With an ad the keyword score is measured against that vacancy instead of a generic skill list.
analyzer.adPlaceholder: Paste the full posting, including the requirements list.
analyzer.shareNote: Shareable for 30 days, scores only — no CV text is stored:

errors.fileUnreadable: That file could not be read.
errors.tooShort: Add the CV text first — at least a few lines are needed to judge anything.
errors.analysisFailed: The analysis could not be completed.
errors.clipboard: The clipboard is not available here. Download the report instead.
errors.shareAuthRequired: Sign in to create a share link. The analysis itself needs no account.
errors.shareEnvMissing: Sharing needs Supabase credentials. Everything else works without them.
errors.shareFailed: The link could not be created. The report is still yours to download.

dataControls.heading: Stored on this device
dataControls.holds: This browser holds {what}. Your CV is not among it: nothing here keeps the document or any line from it.
dataControls.confirm: Deleting removes {what}. It cannot be undone.
dataControls.deleted: Deleted {count} records. This browser now holds nothing from this site.

rewriteDiff.heading: Rewrite weak bullets
rewriteDiff.lede: The local model restates {count, plural, one {# responsibility bullet} other {# responsibility bullets}} as claims. Invented facts are filtered out before you see them; everything unknown stays a visible [quantify: …].
rewriteDiff.nothingUsable: The model returned nothing usable. The deterministic drafts below still work.
rewriteDiff.stale: The text changed since this proposal was made; regenerate the proposals.

keywordPanel.headingBaseline: Skill terms found in the CV
keywordPanel.tierPreferred: Nice to have according to the ad
keywordPanel.noTerms: No recognisable skill terms. Name the tools and methods you work with.
keywordPanel.pasteAd: Paste a job ad to replace this inventory with a real match score against one vacancy.
keywordPanel.titlePartial: PARTIAL: the CV says something close - "{passage}" ({percent}% similar)

reportChat.heading: Ask about this report
reportChat.lede: The local model answers from the report below your score - not from the CV, and not from anything beyond what the checks found.
reportChat.noAnswer: No answer - see the error below.
reportChat.placeholder: Why did keywords cost so much?

fixList.emptyBody: Every check passed. Run the CV against the next job ad to see how the keyword match holds up.
fixList.heading: What to fix, most expensive first
fixList.summary: {count, plural, one {# finding} other {# findings}} · {points} pts
fixList.showLine: Show this line in the parsed text

aiStatus.detecting: Checking what this machine can run locally…
aiStatus.heading: Text model
aiStatus.lede: Rewriting and explanations need a text model. Every option runs on your machine; none of them sees your CV until you ask for one of them.
aiStatus.ollamaUnreachable: Ollama did not answer on localhost:11434. Start it, and set OLLAMA_ORIGINS to include this site.

aiConsent.readyDetail: Hints below run locally against the parsed text; scores are unaffected.
aiConsent.heading: Semantic hints (optional)
aiConsent.lede: A small language model can point out near-misses the literal matcher cannot see - like a CV saying “Postgres” where the ad says “PostgreSQL”. It runs entirely in your browser ({model}, about {sizeMb} MB, downloaded once and cached). Your CV text is never sent anywhere, and scores never change - hints are advice, not measurement.
aiConsent.downloadFailed: The model could not be downloaded.

benchPreview.caption: A real report, ordered by what each fix is worth.

columns.title: Two columns break the text layer

kubernetes.title: "Kubernetes" never appears
kubernetes.evidence: the ad names it four times, twice under requirements

coverageMap.heading: What the CV never addresses
coverageMap.lede: The ad in {chunks, plural, one {# chunk} other {# chunks}}, each compared against the whole CV by the local model. These stay below {threshold}% similarity to anything you wrote. Advice, not measurement - the score is unchanged.
coverageMap.allCovered: Every part of the ad has a close counterpart in the CV.

findingExplain.error: The model could not answer - try again

fixDrafts.heading: Rewrite drafts
fixDrafts.ledeBefore: Responsibility phrasing rewritten as a claim.
fixDrafts.ledeAfter: marks the part only you can fill in. Applying a draft re-runs the analysis so the score rail shows the difference.
fixDrafts.more: {count} more drafts appear as you resolve these.

documentIntake.formats: PDF, DOCX or plain text, up to 10 MB. It is read in this browser and never sent anywhere.

sharedReport.lede: Scores and advice only. The CV itself was never stored.
